items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the environmental conservation law, in relation to including
the Asian longhorned tick on the invasive species list; and the agriculture
and markets law, in relation to requiring the preparation of recommendations
for best practices in treating livestock and farm properties for Asian
longhorned tick treatment, prevention, and management
items.lawCode: Add §9-1711, En Con L; amd §16, Ag & Mkts L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4876

SPONSOR: METZGER
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the environmental conservation law, in
relation to including the Asian longhorned tick on the invasive species
list; and the agriculture and markets law, in relation to requiring the
preparation of recommendations for best practices in treating livestock
and farm properties for Asian longhorned tick treatment, prevention, and
management

 
PURPOSE:

To reduce exposure to a new invasive species, the Asian longhorned tick,
on livestock and farm properties, and thereby reduce incidence of tick-
borne diseases and livestock death, through the development and
promotion of best practices.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one establishes the legislative findings.

Section two adds a new section 9-1711 to the Environmental Conservation
Law which requires that the commissioner of the Department of Environ-
mental Conservation (DEC) add the Asian longhorned tick to the state
invasive species list and include the species in the comprehensive plan
for invasive species management. The commissioner of the DEC, in consul-
tation with the commissioner of the Department of Agriculture and
Markets and Department of Health shall include information on the Asian
longhorned tick on statewide databases and clearinghouses that incorpo-
rates existing data from agencies and organizations in the state, as
well as from nearby states, provinces, Canada, and the federal govern-
ment.

Section three adds a new subdivision 50 to the Agriculture and Markets
Law which directs the commissioner develop recommendations for treat-
ment, prevention and management of livestock and farm property against
Asian longhorned ticks. The recommendations shall develop and distribute
to farmers a pamphlet on Asian longhorned tick treatment, management,
and prevention.

Section four sets forth the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Asian longhorned tick is the first new invasive species to enter the
United States in so, years. Asian longhorned ticks are currently found
in seven states including parts of New York, and as the climate contin-
ues to warm, their geographic reach will continue to expand across the
Eastern Seaboard. This new species can rapidly reproduce asexually,
laying thousands after a single feed. They are attracted to and can
transmit diseases to livestock such as sheep, cattle, and horses. In
Asia, the species carries a virus that kills 15 percent of victims
through, through hemorrhaging, organ failure, and blood loss.

Due to the significant risks that these invasive pests may have on the
livestock industry, farmers need to be made aware of the dangers and be
provided with a reliable source of information to turn to when looking
for answers on how to best protect their properties.  They should be
aware of active ingredients approved by the EPA and DEC, as well as
natural remedies and land care practices that are most effective in tick
prevention to better protect livestock, people, and pets from exposure.

In order to raise awareness for appropriate and effective methods and to
facilitate the delivery of valuable information, this bill requires the
Commissioner of Agriculture and Markets to develop recommendations for
best practices in treating farm properties for Haemaphysalis longicornis
tick prevention and management-the goal ultimately being to rid communi-
ties of ticks that contribute to tick-borne infections.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Minimal

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the fifteenth of April next succeeding the
date on which it shall have become a law. Effective immediately, the
addition, amendment and/or repeal of any rule or regulation necessary
for the implementation of this act on its effective date are authorized
to be made and completed on or before such effective date.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 58 Chapter 674
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 4876-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  amend  the agriculture and markets law, in relation to
        requiring the preparation of recommendations for best  practices
        in  treating  livestock and farm properties for Asian longhorned
        tick treatment, prevention, and management"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This bill would authorize the Department of Agriculture and Markets to
develop best management practices  for  the  treatment,  prevention  and
management of livestock and property to protect against Asian longhorned
ticks.  Though this species of ticks is not specific to livestock, farm-
ers may  benefit  from  guidance  on  landscape  techniques  helpful  in
preventing  the  spread of this tick. Minor amendments are needed to the
original bill in order to substitute cross-references  to  the  Environ-
mental  Conservation Law and to provide the Department with clear direc-
tion on the development of the best management practices.  These  amend-
ments  have  been  agreed  upon by the Executive and the Legislature and
subject to that agreement, I am signing this bill.
 
  This bill is approved.                      (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                                ______
